senses.en_definition: The United States of America, a country in North America whose capital is Washington, D.C.
The Americas, comprising North America, Central America, and South America.

messages.en: My older sister's going to study in the States next year. That's pretty far away, isn't it?
Yeah, it is. Which state is she going to? Has she got a place at a university yet?
California. She's got an offer, and now she's sorting out her visa.

senses.en_definition: A person's son or daughter, regardless of age.

collocations.en: a child who has not yet started school

senses.en_definition: A person originally from a particular state or region.

collocations.en: a native; someone born and raised locally

senses.en_definition: In fixed expressions, a smaller thing of its kind or a small component of a larger whole.

messages.en: Is your kid asleep yet? Mine still wants to play, even though there's school tomorrow.
Not yet. Same here! I've already turned off the TV, and now he wants me to read with him.

senses.en_definition: My child; my son or daughter.
An affectionate form of address to one's own child or a younger person.

messages.en: My little one read a whole storybook all on their own today 🥹 Wouldn't even let me help!
Wow, no wonder you're such a proud mum! I'll get them a new book next time.

collocations.en: to look after his or her child

messages.en: Kak Lina said her child's already asleep.
Oh, let's keep our voices down here, then.
